See: al-Durr al-manthur: 8/365.]]. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: it is Medinan except for one verse, which is His saying: "So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one" [[The author of Zad al-Masir said (8/427): There are three opinions regarding Surat al-Insan. The first: that it is entirely Medinan, said by the majority, including Mujahid and Qatadah. The second: that it is Meccan, said by Ibn Yasar and Muqatil, and reported from Ibn Abbas. The third: that it contains both Meccan and Medinan parts, and on this there are two views: one, that the Meccan part is one verse, namely His saying (Exalted is He): "and do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one," and the rest is entirely Medinan, said by al-Hasan and Ikrimah; the other, that its beginning is Medinan up to His saying (Exalted is He): "Indeed, We have sent down to you the Qur'an," and from this verse to its end is Meccan, related by al-Mawardi.]]. ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] mentioned?﴾ [He means] Adam, peace be upon him. [It was] forty years, [during which he was] a figure of clay between Mecca and al-Ta'if, before the soul was breathed into him. ﴿He was not a thing mentioned﴾: he was not mentioned, nor was he known, nor was it known what his name was or what was intended by it. He means: he was a thing, but was not a thing mentioned, and that was from the time He created him from clay until the soul was breathed into him.

It is related that Umar heard a man recite this verse as: "he was not a thing mentioned," and Umar said: "Would that it had been completed," meaning: would that he had remained in what he was [[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-manthur: 8/366, attributing it to Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ubayd in his "Fada'il", Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]. Ibn Abbas said: then He created him after one hundred and twenty years.

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾, meaning the children of Adam, ﴿from a drop of mixed fluid﴾, meaning: the semen of the man and the semen of the woman.

﴿Amshaj﴾: mixtures. Its singular is *mashj* and *mashij*, like *khidn* and *khadin* (companion).

Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: it means the water of the man [and the water of the woman], which mix in the womb, and from them the child comes into being. The water of the man is white and thick, and the water of the woman is yellow and thin. Whichever of the two overcomes the other, the resemblance is to it. What is of sinew and bone is from the drop of the man, and what is of flesh, blood and hair is from the water of the woman [[See al-Tibyan fi aqsam al-Qur'an by Ibn al-Qayyim, pp. 334-338; Khalq al-insan by Dr. Muhammad Ali al-Bar, p. 390 and following.]].

Al-Dahhak said: by *amshaj* He intended the difference in the colours of the drop: the man's drop is white, red and yellow, and the woman's drop is green and red [and yellow]. [[Omitted from "b".]] This is also the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Likewise al-Kalbi said: *amshaj* is whiteness mixed with redness and yellowness. Yaman said: any two colours that mix are *amshaj*. Ibn Mas'ud said: they are the veins that are in the drop.

Al-Hasan said: a drop mixed with blood, which is the blood of menstruation; when she conceives, menstruation ceases.

Qatadah said: they are the stages of creation: a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then [bone], which He then clothes with flesh, then He brings it into being as another creation [[Ibn Jarir, after citing the above opinions, preferred (29/203-205): "The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who said: the meaning is (from a drop of mixed fluids) the drop of the man and the drop of the woman, because God described the drop as *amshaj*, and when it moves and becomes a clot, it has changed from the meaning of a drop, so how could it be a mixed drop when it is a clot? As for those who said the man's drop is white and red, what is known of the man's drop is that it is of one colour, white inclining to red, and if it is one colour it is not multiple colours. I think those who said they are the veins in the drop intended this meaning."]].

﴿We will test him﴾: We will examine him with commands and prohibitions. ﴿So We made him hearing and seeing﴾. Some grammarians of Arabic said: there is inversion in it; its sense is "so We made him hearing and seeing in order that We might test him," because testing does not occur except after the completion of creation [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/214.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verses 3–4:

﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾, i.e., We made clear to him the way of truth and falsehood, of guidance and misguidance, and We made known to him the path of good and evil. ﴿Either grateful or ungrateful﴾: either a believer who is fortunate, or a disbeliever who is wretched. It was also said: the meaning of the statement is conditional, i.e., We made the way clear to him whether he gives thanks or disbelieves. [See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra': 3/214.] Then He explained what awaits each of the two groups, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains﴾, i.e., in Hell. The people of Madinah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read "salasilа" (salāsilā) and "qawarira" (qawārīrā) with a final alif in pause (waqf, stopping at the end of a word) and with tanwin (nunation) in continuation (wasl, joining words). In both words they all did this. Hamzah and Ya'qub read without the alif in pause and without tanwin in continuation in both words. Ibn Kathir read the first "qawarira" with the alif in pause and with tanwin in continuation, while "salasila" and the second "qawarira" were read without alif and without tanwin. Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs read "salasilа" and the first "qawarira" with the alif [in pause] [[addition from "b".]] according to the script, and without tanwin in continuation, while the second "qawarira" was read without alif and without tanwin. His statement ﴿and shackles﴾, i.e., on their hands, which are chained to their necks. ﴿And a blazing fire﴾, i.e., a fierce, kindled flame.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 76, verses 5–8:

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ means the believers who are truthful in their faith and obedient to their Lord. Their singular is *barr* (بَارٌّ), like *shahid* (شَاهِدٍ) and *ashhad* (أَشْهَادٍ), and *nasir* (نَاصِرٍ) and *ansar* (أَنْصَارٍ). *Barr* (بَرُّ) is also used like *nahr* (نَهَرٍ) and *anhar* (أَنْهَارٍ). [In manuscript "A", the reading is "wahiduhā" (واحدها).] ﴿They will drink﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿from a cup﴾ [in manuscript "B", the reading is "fīhi" (فيه)] containing a drink ﴿whose mixture is camphor.﴾ Qatadah said: it is mixed for them with camphor and sealed with musk. Ikrimah said: "its mixture" means its taste. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: it means like camphor in its whiteness, its fragrant scent, and its coolness, because camphor is not drunk. This is like His saying: ﴿until, when he made it fire﴾ [Al-Kahf 18:96], meaning like fire. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatadah [in manuscript "B", it is Muqatil; the correct reading is what we have recorded from manuscript "A", as in al-Tabari 29/207] and Mujahid: its scent is mixed with the scent of camphor. Ibn Kaysan said: it is perfumed with camphor, musk, and ginger. Ata' and al-Kalbi said: "Kafur" is the name of a spring of water in Paradise.

﴿A spring﴾ is in the accusative, following *al-kafur*. It was also said that it is in the accusative as an expression of praise. It was also said: I mean, a spring. Al-Zajjaj said: the best view is that the meaning is "from a spring" ﴿from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [in manuscript "A" it is omitted: "yashrabuha" (يشربها)], and the *ba'* (بَاءُ) is redundant (silah), and it was said that it means "from it." ﴿The servants of Allah﴾: Ibn Abbas said: they are the friends of Allah. ﴿They make it gush forth abundantly﴾ meaning they lead it wherever they wish from their dwellings and palaces, like one who has a river that he channels here and there to wherever he wants.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾: this is one of their attributes in the world, meaning they were like that in the world.

Qatadah said: He means they fulfil what Allah has obligated upon them of prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, 'umrah, and other obligations. [Recorded by al-Tabari 29/208, and by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir 2/336.] The meaning of *nadhr* (نَذْر) is obligation.

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: when they vow in obedience to Allah, they fulfil it.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Talhah ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Ayli, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him." [Recorded by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta' 2/476, in the Book of Vows and Oaths, chapter on what is not permissible of vows in disobedience to Allah. It is part of a hadith recorded by al-Bukhari in the Book of Oaths and Vows, chapter on vowing in obedience, 11/581, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/20–21.]

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾: spreading, extended. It is said: *istatara al-subh* (اسْتَطَارَ الصُّبْحُ), when the dawn extends and spreads.

Muqatil said: its evil will be widespread in the heavens, so they will be split open, the stars will be scattered, the sun and moon will be wrapped up, and the angels will be terrified. On the earth, the mountains will be blown away, the waters will vanish, and everything on the earth, mountain or building, will be shattered.

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾: meaning despite their love for food, its scarcity, their desire for it, and their need for it. It was also said: out of love for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿To the needy﴾: the poor who has no wealth; ﴿and the orphan﴾: the young one who has no father; ﴿and the captive.﴾ Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ata' said: he is the prisoner from among the people of the qiblah (the Muslims). Qatadah said: Allah commanded that captives be treated well, and their captives on that day were from the people of polytheism. It was also said: the captive is the slave. It was also said: the woman, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are with you as 'awan (captives/helpers)." [A part of a hadith recorded by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar 3/212, and by al-Tirmidhi in the Chapters on Suckling, chapter on what has come concerning the rights of a wife over her husband, 4/326, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Majah recorded it with similar wording in the Book of Marriage, no. 1851, 1/594. Imam Muslim recorded its meaning in the hadith of Jabir concerning the Farewell Pilgrimage. It has a supporting narration from the paternal uncle of Abu Hurrah al-Raqashi, in Imam Ahmad 5/72–73. See Irwa' al-Ghalil 7/53–54, 96–97.] That is, captives.

They differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who fed a needy person, an orphan, and a captive on a single day. [Mentioned by the author of al-Zad al-Masir 8/432.]

Mujahid and Ata' narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). The reason was that he worked for a Jew for some barley. [In manuscript "B", the following is omitted: "faqabada al-sha'ir" (فَقَبَضَ الشَّعِيرَ).] He ground a third of it, and they made some of it for themselves to eat. When it was fully cooked, a needy person came and asked, so they gave him the food. Then they worked the second third, and when it was fully cooked, an orphan came and asked, so they fed him. Then they worked the remaining third, and when it was fully cooked, a captive from the polytheists came and asked, so they fed him, and they spent that day hungry. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah that the captive was from the people of polytheism. In this is evidence that feeding captives, even if they are from the people of polytheism, is good and its reward is hoped for. [Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 180: "Al-Tha'labi narrated it through al-Qasim ibn Bahram from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, and through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas… al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi said: among the hadiths that hearts reject is a hadith they narrated from Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it… then he said: this is a fabricated, contrived hadith that deceives only a fool. Ibn al-Jawzi recorded it in al-Mawdu'at and said: there is no doubt that it is fabricated." See al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 516. And review what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) wrote in Minhaj al-Sunnah 7/174–187, in his refutation of Ibn al-Mutahhar regarding the argument based on such narrations, where he clarified its invalidity in thirteen ways. See also Tafsir al-Qurtubi 19/130–135.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verses 9–12:**

﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They did not actually say this aloud, but Allah knew it from their hearts, so He praised them for it.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a day that is grim.﴾ On it, faces will frown because of its terror and severity. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 19–21:

﴿And there will go around them youths made eternal. When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.﴾ ʿAṭāʾ said: He means in the whiteness and beauty of pearls. And pearls, when scattered from the string onto a carpet, are more beautiful than when strung together. The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: They were likened to scattered pearls only because of their dispersal in service; had they been in a row, they would have been likened to strung pearls.

﴿And when you look there﴾, i.e., when you look with your eyes and gaze there, meaning in Paradise, ﴿you will see bliss﴾ that cannot be described, ﴿and a great dominion﴾. This is that the lowest in rank among them looks upon his dominion over a distance of a thousand years, seeing its farthest extent as he sees its nearest. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It is that the messenger of the Lord of Might among the angels does not enter upon him except with his permission. It was also said: a dominion that has no end.

﴿Upon them will be garments of green silk and brocade.﴾ Ahl al-Madina and Hamza read ʿĀliyahum with a sukun on the yāʾ and a kasra on the hāʾ, so it is in the place of a nominative as the subject of an initial clause, and its predicate is "garments of silk." The others read it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and a ḍamma on the hāʾ, as an adjective (ṣifa), meaning "above them," and it is accusative as an adverb of place (ẓarf). [In "A" it reads: as a state (ḥāl), and ʿāliyahum: i.e., above them, and it may be accusative as an adverb of place.] ﴿garments of green silk and brocade﴾. Nafi' and Hafs read "khuḍrun wa-istabraqun" [in "A": both in the nominative], conjoined to "al-thiyāb" (garments). Hamza and al-Kisa'i read both in the genitive. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read "khuḍrin" in the genitive and "istabraqun" in the nominative. Abu Ja'far and the people of Basra and Syria read in the opposite manner: the nominative for "khuḍrun" as an adjective of "al-thiyāb," and the genitive "khuḍrin" as an adjective of "sundus," and "istabraqun" in the nominative as conjoined to "thiyābu istabraq," the construction having dropped the first noun and placed the second in its position, as in His saying "and ask the village" (i.e., the people of the village), and similarly His saying "khazz" (i.e., garment of khazz). As for the genitive of "istabraq," it is conjoined to "sundus," and it is genitive by the annexation of "garments" to it; the two are two kinds, and the garments are annexed to both, as you say "a garment of khazz and cotton," annexing it to the two kinds. [Text between the brackets is absent from "B".]

﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink.﴾ It was said: pure, free from impurities and filth, not defiled by hands and feet as the wine of this world is.

Abu Qilaba and Ibrahim said: it does not turn into impure urine, but turns into perspiration in their bodies, its scent like the scent of musk. That is because they are brought food, and when that is finished they are brought the pure drink; they drink it, it purifies their bellies, and what they ate turns into perspiration exiting their skins, [a scent] more fragrant than pungent musk, and their bellies become slender and their appetite returns. [The word "scent" is absent from "B".]

Muqatil said: it is a spring of water at the gate of Paradise; whoever drinks from it, Allah removes whatever rancor, deceit and envy was in his heart.

﴿And when you look there﴾, i.e., when you look with your eyes and gaze there, meaning in Paradise, ﴿you will see bliss﴾ that cannot be described, ﴿and a great dominion﴾. This is that the lowest in rank among them looks upon his dominion over a distance of a thousand years, seeing its farthest extent as he sees its nearest. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It is that the messenger of the Lord of Might among the angels does not enter upon him except with his permission. It was also said: a dominion that has no end.

﴿Upon them will be garments of green silk and brocade.﴾ Ahl al-Madina and Hamza read ʿĀliyahum with a sukun on the yāʾ and a kasra on the hāʾ, so it is in the place of a nominative as the subject of an initial clause, and its predicate is "garments of silk." The others read it with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and a ḍamma on the hāʾ, as an adjective (ṣifa), meaning "above them," and it is accusative as an adverb of place (ẓarf). [In "A" it reads: as a state (ḥāl), and ʿāliyahum: i.e., above them, and it may be accusative as an adverb of place.] ﴿garments of green silk and brocade﴾. Nafi' and Hafs read "khuḍrun wa-istabraqun" [in "A": both in the nominative], conjoined to "al-thiyāb" (garments). Hamza and al-Kisa'i read both in the genitive. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read "khuḍrin" in the genitive and "istabraqun" in the nominative. Abu Ja'far and the people of Basra and Syria read in the opposite manner: the nominative for "khuḍrun" as an adjective of "al-thiyāb," and the genitive "khuḍrin" as an adjective of "sundus," and "istabraqun" in the nominative as conjoined to "thiyābu istabraq," the construction having dropped the first noun and placed the second in its position, as in His saying "and ask the village" (i.e., the people of the village), and similarly His saying "khazz" (i.e., garment of khazz). As for the genitive of "istabraq," it is conjoined to "sundus," and it is genitive by the annexation of "garments" to it; the two are two kinds, and the garments are annexed to both, as you say "a garment of khazz and cotton," annexing it to the two kinds. [Text between the brackets is absent from "B".]

﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink.﴾ It was said: pure, free from impurities and filth, not defiled by hands and feet as the wine of this world is.

Abu Qilaba and Ibrahim said: it does not turn into impure urine, but turns into perspiration in their bodies, its scent like the scent of musk. That is because they are brought food, and when that is finished they are brought the pure drink; they drink it, it purifies their bellies, and what they ate turns into perspiration exiting their skins, [a scent] more fragrant than pungent musk, and their bellies become slender and their appetite returns. [The word "scent" is absent from "B".]

Muqatil said: it is a spring of water at the gate of Paradise; whoever drinks from it, Allah removes whatever rancor, deceit and envy was in his heart.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verses 22–24:

﴿Indeed, this was a reward for you, and your striving has been appreciated.﴾ That is: what has been described of the bliss of Paradise was a reward for you for your deeds. ﴿And your striving﴾ — your deeds in the world in obedience to God — ﴿has been appreciated.﴾ Ata' said: "I will thank you for it [and so reward you]" [[In "B" it reads: "so I give you"]] with the best of rewards.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, We Ourselves have sent down the Qur'an to you in gradual revelation.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: "Dispersed, verse after verse; it was not sent down all at once."

﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, and do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one.﴾ That is, from among the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Sinner or ungrateful one﴾ — that is, "or ungrateful," and the alif is a silah (a superfluous particle that adds no meaning).

Qatadah said: "By the sinner and the ungrateful one he meant Abu Jahl. When prayer was enjoined upon the Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Jahl forbade him from it and said: 'If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely trample his neck'" [[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/339, and al-Tabari: 29/224. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/378 to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]].

Muqatil said: "By 'the sinner' he meant Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and by 'the ungrateful one' al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. They said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'If you did what you did for the sake of women and wealth, then turn back from this matter.' Utbah said: 'I will marry you to my daughter and bring her to you without a dowry.' al-Walid said: 'I will give you wealth until you are content, so turn back from this matter.' Then God revealed this verse" [[al-Alusi said: 29/165–166: "The intended meaning of 'the sinner' and 'the ungrateful one' is their category. Attaching the prohibition to these two indicates that the two descriptions are its cause; so the prohibition must be against obeying in sin and disbelief, not in what is neither sin nor disbelief. The meaning is: do not obey one who commits sin and invites you to it, or one who commits disbelief and invites you to it; that is, do not follow any sinner when he invites you to sin, or any ungrateful one when he invites you to disbelief. For when it is said, 'Do not obey the oppressor,' what is understood is: do not follow him in oppression when he invites you to it. Denying this understanding is obstinacy.' It was also said: 'The sinner is Utbah and the ungrateful one is al-Walid, but the first view stated above is more appropriate.' He also said: 'Prohibiting this even though the Prophet is protected from such error guides others who are not protected to humble themselves before God and to seek of Him protection from falling into what is not fitting.']].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verses 25–28:

﴿And mention the name of your Lord morning and evening. And during part of the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him through the long night.﴾ [I.e., the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers.] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "b".]] ﴿And glorify Him through the long night﴾ means the voluntary prayer after the obligatory prayer.

﴿Indeed, these [people]﴾ means the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿love the immediate [life]﴾, i.e., the immediate abode, which is this world.

﴿And they leave behind them﴾ means in front of them ﴿a heavy Day﴾, severe, which is the Day of Resurrection. That is, they abandon it, so they do not believe in it and do not work for it.

﴿We created them and strengthened﴾ [We made strong and firm] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "b".]] ﴿their frame﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah [and Muqatil] [[omitted from "a".]] said: "Asrahum" means their creation; it is said: "a man of good asr", i.e., good build.

Al-Hasan said: it means that He joined their joints to one another with the veins and sinews.

It is narrated from Mujahid, regarding the interpretation of "al-asr", that he said: it is the shalaj, meaning the place where the two passages of urine and feces are; when the filth exits, they contract.

﴿And if We wish, We can replace them with others like them, a [complete] replacement﴾. That is: if We wish, We destroy them and bring others resembling them, and make them a replacement for them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 29–31:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ — meaning this surah — ﴿is a reminder﴾, an admonition and an exhortation. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, a means through obedience.

﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., the polytheists, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment.﴾
